newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end lower on rate worries.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end lower on rate worries.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended lower on Thursday amid concerns over a possible rise in Japanese interest rates following reports of comments by a senior official at Japan's Ministry of Finance.
Eisuke Sakakibara was quoted by Thursday's Nikkei Financial Daily as saying the Japanese economy was stronger than the market thought and also that the dollar's correction was about to finish.
The remarks sparked a sharp fall in the dollar and a slide in Euroyen and Japanese government bond futures.
"The comments took a while to sink in, but now seem to be the reason the market has fallen," said one Singapore-based Japanese futures trader.

The benchmark Nikkei 225 December contract closed 240 points lower at 20,840. It earlier rose to a high of 21,260 on a follow-through of positive sentiment generated by Bill Clinton's as-expected victory in the U.S. presidential election.
"Sakakibara's comments could be seen as negative for stocks if they encourage a strong correction in the yen," said a dealer in Singapore.
Chartists said the December Nikkei future contract should find support around 20,800 points.
On the upside, it would need to close above 21,130 to see further gains and above 21,300 to negate its recent downtrend.
